1910.08.d: In Xuantong 2 the Qing government pursued the “New Policies” and “preparatory constitutionalism”, and the provincial assemblies jointly petitioned for the speedy convening of a parliament. The realm comprised the eighteen provinces inside the Great Wall, the three northeastern provinces and Xinjiang, with Inner and Outer Mongolia, Qinghai and Xizang as dependencies; Zhao Erfeng replaced the native chieftains with appointed officials in the Sichuan Frontier, the Sichuan Army entered Lhasa in February, and the 13th Dalai Lama fled to India. Taiwan, the Kwantung Leased Territory, Jiaozhou Bay, Weihaiwei, Guangzhouwan and Hong Kong had been seized or forcibly leased by the Powers. On 22 August Japan annexed Korea; France had seized Indochina and the Netherlands the East Indies, and Britain and Russia had partitioned their spheres of influence in Central Asia under the Anglo-Russian Convention of 1907.
1910.08.t: Late-Qing New Policies · Japan annexes Korea

1911.10.d: In April the Tongmenghui's Guangzhou Uprising (Huanghuagang Uprising) failed; in May the Qing government formed the “Cabinet of Imperial Kinsmen” and proclaimed the “nationalization of the railways”, and the Railway Protection Movement in Sichuan grew into an armed uprising. On 10 October the New Army rose in Wuchang and set up the Hubei Military Government, and the 1911 Revolution broke out; the Beiyang Army moved south, fierce fighting raged at Yangxia, and the Qing court was forced to recall Yuan Shikai. Within the month Hunan, Shaanxi (on the 22nd), Jiujiang and Nanchang in Jiangxi, Taiyuan in Shanxi and Kunming in Yunnan were recovered one after another. Meanwhile the Italo-Turkish War was at its height, with Italy seizing Ottoman Libya; tsarist Russia and Britain were biding their time in Outer Mongolia and Xizang.

1911.12.d: In November Shanghai, Guizhou, Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Guangxi, Anhui, Guangdong, Fujian and Sichuan declared independence one after another, breaking away from the Qing government; Shandong's independence was soon revoked. Qing forces burned and looted Hankou on 1 November and took Hanyang on the 27th; on 2 December the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Allied Army recovered Nanjing, the North and South agreed a ceasefire and opened peace talks in Shanghai, and on the 29th the provincial delegates elected Sun Yat-sen Provisional President. Qing forces broke through Niangzi Pass and entered Taiyuan. Instigated by tsarist Russia, the Outer Mongolian princes declared “independence” on 1 December, and on the 29th the Jebtsundamba Khutughtu proclaimed himself Bogd Khan. In the same month King George V held his Coronation Durbar in Delhi and announced the transfer of the capital to Delhi; the Persian parliament was dissolved under a tsarist Russian ultimatum.

1912.02.d: On 1 January Sun Yat-sen was sworn in as Provisional President in Nanjing and the Republic of China was founded; the Luanzhou Uprising failed, and the Northern Expedition Army took Suzhou (Anhui). On 12 February the Qing emperor abdicated, ending the rule of the Qing dynasty; on the 15th the Senate elected Yuan Shikai Provisional President; at the end of the month a mutiny broke out in Beijing, and Yuan used it as a pretext not to come south, usurping the fruits of the 1911 Revolution. Turmoil on the frontiers: the Ili Uprising set up the Xin-Yi Grand Military Governorate; Hulunbuir, instigated by tsarist Russia, drove out the Qing officials and attached itself to Outer Mongolia; the Uliassutai General was expelled; the Sichuan Army in Lhasa mutinied, and the Dalai Lama called from India for the “expulsion of the Han”. In the same period tsarist Russian troops suppressed the constitutionalists of Tabriz in Persia.
1912.02.t: Founding of the Republic of China · Abdication of the Qing emperor

1913.08.d: In April 1912 the Provisional Government moved north, and in August the Kuomintang was founded. In March 1913 Yuan Shikai had Song Jiaoren assassinated, and in April he signed the Reorganization Loan; in July Li Liejun raised troops at Hukou and Sun Yat-sen launched the Second Revolution, with Jiangsu, Anhui, Shanghai, Guangdong, Fujian, Hunan and Chongqing rising against Yuan one after another; by the end of August most had been defeated, and only He Haiming in Nanjing and Xiong Kewu in Chongqing still held out. Outer Mongolia had taken Kobdo in 1912 and in 1913 invaded Inner Mongolia along five routes; at the end of 1912 the Sichuan Army was driven out of Lhasa and the Dalai Lama returned to Xizang. Meanwhile the two Balkan Wars cost the Ottoman Empire most of its European territory; in July 1912 Emperor Taishō of Japan ascended the throne.

1914.11.d: In September 1913 Nanjing fell and the Second Revolution failed; in October Yuan Shikai was formally elected President, then dissolved the Kuomintang and suspended parliament, and in 1914 he abolished the Provisional Constitution, retitled the provincial military governors as generals and ruled as a dictator. The Bai Lang Uprising army fought its way across Henan, Hubei, Shaanxi and Gansu and was defeated in August. In November 1913 the Sino-Russian Declaration recognized Outer Mongolian “autonomy”, and the Mongolian troops withdrew from Inner Mongolia; in April 1914 tsarist Russia forcibly placed Tannu Uriankhai under its “protection”; Britain engineered the Simla Conference and concocted the illegal “McMahon Line”; the Chinese side refused to sign. When the First World War broke out, Japan, on the pretext of declaring war on Germany, sent troops into Shandong and seized Qingdao by force on 7 November. Meanwhile the Ottoman Empire entered the war, and Japan seized Germany's South Seas Islands.
1914.11.t: Outbreak of the First World War · Japan seizes Qingdao

1915.06.d: In January Japan presented the Twenty-One Demands; to win Japanese support for his bid to become emperor, Yuan Shikai accepted the ultimatum on 9 May (Group V being left for future negotiation), and boycotts of Japanese goods spread everywhere. On 7 June China, Russia and Mongolia signed the Kyakhta Agreement: Outer Mongolia renounced its “independence” and practised “autonomy” under the suzerainty of the Republic of China, and the Beijing government stationed officials in Urga. Chen Yi led the Beiyang Army into Sichuan to govern it, and the provinces under Yuan Shikai's control reached their greatest extent. Meanwhile Anglo-French forces landed at Gallipoli in April, and the Ottoman Empire began the mass deportation and massacre of the Armenians.

1915.12.d: In August the Peace Planning Society promoted a monarchy, the provincial “citizens' representatives” unanimously “acclaimed” Yuan emperor, and on 12 December Yuan Shikai announced that he accepted the throne, restoring the monarchy and naming the following year “Hongxian 1”. On 5 December the uprising on the warship Zhaohe in Shanghai failed; Liang Qichao wrote against the monarchy, Cai E slipped back to Yunnan, and on the 25th Tang Jiyao and Cai E declared Yunnan independent and organized the National Protection Army to fight Yuan, and the National Protection War broke out. In November China and Russia signed an agreement making Hulunbuir a special region. Meanwhile British Indian forces were besieged by the Ottoman army at Kut in Mesopotamia, and the Allies began to evacuate Gallipoli.

1916.05.d: In January the National Protection Army entered Sichuan and attacked Xuzhou (Sichuan) and Luzhou, fighting the Beiyang Army to a stalemate at Naxi and Mianhuapo, while the Guizhou Army pushed east into western Hunan. Guizhou (27 January) and Guangxi (15 March) declared independence one after another, and on 22 March Yuan Shikai was forced to abolish the monarchy. In April Guangdong and Zhejiang declared independence; on 8 May the independent provinces set up the Military Affairs Council at Zhaoqing, and Shaanxi, Sichuan and Hunan followed; the Chinese Revolutionary Army held Weixian, and Zhang Zuolin drove out Duan Zhigui and took control of Fengtian. On 6 June Yuan Shikai died amid the execration of the whole nation. Meanwhile the British garrison at Kut surrendered in April, and in May Britain and France signed the Sykes–Picot Agreement partitioning the Ottoman Empire's Asian territories.
1916.05.t: National Protection War · Military Affairs Council

1917.07.d: After Yuan Shikai's death the Beiyang warlords split up, each faction backed by imperialist powers. On 1 July Zhang Xun restored Puyi to the throne; Duan Qirui held an oath-taking rally of his troops at Machang on the 3rd, and the Anti-Restoration Army fought its way into Beijing on the 12th, the restoration collapsing after twelve days. Duan Qirui regained control of the Beijing government and refused to restore the parliament and the Provisional Constitution; Li Yuanhong left office and Feng Guozhang became acting President. Sun Yat-sen went south to Guangzhou and launched the Constitution Protection Movement; Lu Rongting of Guangdong and Guangxi declared autonomy, and Tang Jiyao of Yunnan responded. In Sichuan, Liu Cunhou and the acting military governor Dai Kan fought street battles in Chengdu, and Dai Kan was defeated and killed. The “autonomous” Outer Mongolia and the Xizang local authorities both lay outside Beijing's jurisdiction. Meanwhile the Russian Provisional Government was plunged into the July crisis, and British forces had occupied Baghdad in March.

1917.11.d: On 14 August the Beijing government declared war on Germany and Austria-Hungary. In September the Extraordinary Session of Parliament in Guangzhou organized the Military Government of the Republic of China, with Sun Yat-sen as Generalissimo, and the Constitution Protection War broke out: Lingling and Hengyang in southern Hunan declared autonomy, the Guangxi Army entered Hunan, Beiyang frontline commanders circulated telegrams calling for a ceasefire, Fu Liangzuo abandoned Changsha and fled, and Duan Qirui resigned on 22 November. In Sichuan the Yunnan and Guizhou National Pacification Armies fought Liu Cunhou and Wu Guangxin, and Mo Qingyu in Chao-Mei sided with the North. The Tibetan army encroached eastward on Kham, attacking Riwoqe and Qamdo. Meanwhile the October Revolution triumphed in Russia on 7 November; the United States and Japan signed the Lansing–Ishii Agreement, and Britain issued the Balfour Declaration.

1918.11.d: Duan Qirui returned to office and pursued “unification by force”: the Beiyang Army retook Yuezhou and Changsha in March and took Hengyang in April; Zhang Jingyao became military governor of Hunan, while Wu Peifu, stationed at Hengyang, ceased fighting. In May the military government, dominated by the Guangxi Clique, was reorganized under a seven-member directorate, Sun Yat-sen was forced out of Guangdong, and the Constitution Protection Movement failed. Xiong Kewu became military governor of Sichuan; National Pacification Armies rose in Shaanxi and western Hubei, and Chen Jiongming's Guangdong Army to Aid Fujian occupied Zhangzhou. The Tibetan army took Qamdo in April; through British “mediation” a ceasefire was agreed in August–October, leaving the area west of the Jinsha River together with Dege and Baiyu in Tibetan army hands. In October Xu Shichang became President. Meanwhile the First World War ended with the armistice of 11 November; Japan sent troops into Siberia in August, and after the Rice Riots at home Hara Takashi formed a cabinet.
1918.11.t: North–South standoff · First World War ends

1919.05.d: The North–South peace talks opened in Shanghai in February and broke down in May, both sides broadly keeping to the ceasefire lines. On 30 April the Paris Peace Conference decided to transfer Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan; on 4 May Beijing students marched in protest and the May Fourth Movement broke out; in June Shanghai workers went on strike and merchants shut their shops, forcing the Beijing government to dismiss Cao Rulin, Zhang Zongxiang and Lu Zongyu, and the Chinese delegation refused to sign the peace treaty with Germany. The May Fourth Movement was the beginning of China's New Democratic Revolution. The Anhui Clique grew powerful through the War Participation Army and the Anfu Parliament, and Wu Peifu of the Zhili Clique telegraphed his opposition. Meanwhile the March First Movement took place in Korea, and the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea was set up in Shanghai; the Amritsar Massacre occurred in India; the Third Anglo-Afghan War broke out.
1919.05.t: May Fourth Movement · Paris Peace Conference

1919.11.d: Xu Shuzheng, as Northwest Frontier Commissioner, led the Frontier Defence Army into Urga; the Outer Mongolian princes petitioned to renounce autonomy, and on 22 November the Beijing government formally abolished Outer Mongolian “autonomy” and restored its jurisdiction; Uriankhai, too, came under the control of Chinese and Mongolian troops. In July Zhang Zuolin drove out Meng Enyuan of Jilin and unified the three northeastern provinces; Altay was merged into Xinjiang. The rift between the Zhili and Anhui Cliques deepened, and Wu Peifu at Hengyang was preparing to withdraw his troops and return north. Within the Constitution Protection camp, the Guangxi Clique and Sun Yat-sen's faction were at odds. Meanwhile in July Soviet Russia issued its first declaration to China (the Karakhan Manifesto), the Red Army advanced east, and Kolchak abandoned Omsk in November.

1920.07.d: In May Wu Peifu withdrew his troops and returned north; the Hunan Army seized the chance to advance north and drove out Zhang Jingyao in June, and in July Tan Yankai issued a circular telegram proclaiming Hunan self-government. On 14 July the Zhili–Anhui War broke out, the first large-scale war among the Beiyang warlords; Wu Peifu routed the Anhui Clique's Frontier Defence Army at Zhuozhou and Gaobeidian, Duan Qirui stepped down, and the Zhili and Fengtian Cliques jointly controlled the Beijing government. The Guangzhou Military Government split, with Sun Yat-sen and Tang Jiyao breaking with the Guangxi Clique; in Sichuan, Xiong Kewu fought Lü Chao and the Yunnan Army for Chengdu. In January the Hulunbuir Special Region was abolished. Meanwhile in April Soviet Russia set up the Far Eastern Republic as a buffer; Japan used the Nikolayevsk Incident as a pretext to occupy northern Sakhalin; French forces captured Damascus in July.

1921.08.d: In autumn 1920 the Guangdong Army returned and drove the Guangxi Clique out of Guangdong, and Sun Yat-sen came back to Guangdong, becoming Extraordinary President in May 1921; in June the Guangdong Army attacked Guangxi and entered Nanning in August, and Lu Rongting fled. The Sichuan Army, having driven out the Yunnan and Guizhou Armies, declared self-government; the Hunan Army's expedition to aid Hubei suffered a setback, and Wu Peifu advanced to occupy Yuezhou; the Zhili Clique entered Shaanxi and expelled Chen Shufan. In July the First National Congress of the CPC was held in Shanghai and the Communist Party of China was born, an epoch-making event. In February Ungern's White Russian forces took Urga; in July the Soviet Russian Red Army and the Mongolian People's Army marched in and set up the Mongolian People's Government, and Outer Mongolia again declared “independence”; in August Tannu Uriankhai declared “independence” with Soviet Russian backing. Meanwhile Reza Khan staged a coup in Iran; the Malabar Uprising broke out in India.
1921.08.t: Founding of the CPC · Guangdong–Guangxi War

1922.06.d: At the end of April came the First Zhili–Fengtian War: the Zhili Clique won at Changxindian and elsewhere, the Fengtian Army withdrew beyond Shanhaiguan, and Zhang Zuolin declared the “autonomy” of the three northeastern provinces; in June Xu Shichang stepped down, Li Yuanhong resumed the presidency, and the Zhili Clique controlled the Beijing government. Feng Yuxiang defeated Zhao Ti, and Henan passed to the Zhili Clique. Sun Yat-sen's Northern Expedition Army entered southern Jiangxi; on 16 June Chen Jiongming rebelled and shelled the Presidential Office, and Sun Yat-sen took refuge aboard the warship Yongfeng. The Guangdong Army withdrew from Guangxi, self-government armies sprang up everywhere, and Li Zongren held Yulin; Yuan Zuming entered Guiyang, and Tang Jiyao regained Kunming. In February the Washington Conference produced the Nine-Power Treaty and the treaty on the Shandong question, and China reverted to joint domination by the Powers. Meanwhile Japan announced that it would withdraw its troops from Siberia within the year.

1923.10.d: In December 1922 Qingdao was returned to China. In January 1923 the Yunnan and Guangxi Armies drove Chen Jiongming out of Guangzhou; Sun Yat-sen returned to Guangdong in February and set up the Generalissimo's Headquarters in March; Chen Jiongming fell back to the Dong River, Deng Benyin held the eight prefectures of the Southern Route, and Shen Hongying rose and attacked Guangzhou but was beaten back to northern Guangxi. In January the Sun–Joffe Manifesto was issued; in February the great strike of the Beijing–Hankou Railway workers was bloodily suppressed by Wu Peifu, resulting in the February 7 Massacre; in June the Zhili Clique drove out Li Yuanhong, and on 5 October Cao Kun was elected President by bribery. The Tan–Zhao War and the Anti-Rebel Campaign in Sichuan followed one after another, and the Yunnan Army entered Guiyang. Meanwhile the Great Kanto earthquake struck Japan on 1 September; in October the Republic of Turkey was founded.
1923.10.t: February 7 Massacre · Cao Kun's election by bribery

1924.06.d: In January the First National Congress of the Kuomintang was held in Guangzhou, establishing the Three Great Policies of alliance with Russia, cooperation with the Communists and assistance to the peasants and workers; the first KMT–CPC cooperation took shape, and with it the National Revolution got under way; on 16 June the Whampoa Military Academy opened. In May China and the Soviet Union signed the Agreement on General Principles and established diplomatic relations. The Sichuan Anti-Rebel Army was defeated; Yang Sen entered Chengdu in February and became military governor in May, and Xiong Kewu withdrew from Sichuan. In Guangxi, Li Zongren and Huang Shaohong formed the Anti-Rebel Army to Pacify Guangxi and entered Nanning, while Lu Rongting was besieged in Guilin by Shen Hongying. Tang Shengzhi held southern Hunan. Lu Yongxiang held Zhejiang, and his relations with Qi Xieyuan of Jiangsu were tense. Meanwhile Lenin died in January; in May the United States passed the Immigration Act excluding the Japanese.

1924.11.d: In September came the Jiangsu–Zhejiang War: Qi Xieyuan and Sun Chuanfang defeated Lu Yongxiang, and Sun Chuanfang gained Zhejiang. In September the Second Zhili–Fengtian War broke out, with the Fengtian Army attacking Jiumenkou and Shanhaiguan; on 23 October Feng Yuxiang turned his troops back and staged the Beijing Coup, imprisoned Cao Kun and organized the Guominjun, and on 5 November expelled Puyi from the Forbidden City; Wu Peifu fled south by sea, and the Zhili government collapsed. On the 24th Duan Qirui took office as Provisional Chief Executive. In October the revolutionary government in Guangzhou put down the Merchants' Corps rebellion; on 13 November Sun Yat-sen left Guangdong for the north, calling for a National Convention and the abolition of the unequal treaties; Lu Rongting stepped down. On the 26th the “Mongolian People's Republic” was founded. Meanwhile Ibn Saud captured Mecca in October.
1924.11.t: Beijing Coup · Sun Yat-sen goes north

1925.07.d: In January the Fengtian Army and Lu Yongxiang moved south and drove out Qi Xieyuan; Zhang Zongchang became military governor of Shandong in April, and the Fengtian Clique's power reached the lower Yangtze; the Guominjun held the capital region, Chahar, Suiyuan, Henan and Shaanxi. In February–March came the First Eastern Expedition, in which the Whampoa student army won victories at Danshui and Mianhu; on 12 March Sun Yat-sen died in Beijing. On 30 May came the May Thirtieth Massacre, and the May Thirtieth Movement swept the country; in June came the Shaji Massacre and the Guangzhou–Hong Kong Strike, and the high tide of the Great Revolution arrived; after the Yang–Liu Rebellion was put down, the Nationalist Government was established in Guangzhou on 1 July. The New Guangxi Clique drove out Shen Hongying, defeated the Yunnan Army and unified Guangxi. Meanwhile Japan and the Soviet Union established diplomatic relations in January, and Japanese troops withdrew from northern Sakhalin in May; in July the Great Syrian Revolt broke out.
1925.07.t: May Thirtieth Movement · Guangzhou Nationalist Government

1925.12.d: In August Liao Zhongkai, leader of the KMT Left, was assassinated by the Right, and Xu Chongzhi left Guangdong. In October Sun Chuanfang drove the Fengtian Army out of Jiangsu and Anhui and formed the Five-Province Allied Army; Wu Peifu proclaimed himself commander-in-chief of the Allied Anti-Rebel Armies in Hankou. The Second Eastern Expedition took Huizhou in October and pacified Chao-Mei in November, and the Southern Expedition army entered the Southern Route. On 22 November Guo Songling rose against Fengtian at Luanzhou and advanced to the Juliu River; on 24 December he was defeated and captured, and was killed the next day; the Guominjun took Tianjin on the 24th, and Li Jinglin and Zhang Zongchang formed the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army. The Guominjun's Liu Yufen entered Gansu and Song Zheyuan entered Rehe; the KMT Right held the Western Hills Conference, opposing KMT–CPC cooperation. Meanwhile in December Reza Khan of Iran ascended the throne as Shah, founding the Pahlavi dynasty.
1925.12.t: Second Eastern Expedition · Guo Songling's revolt against Fengtian

1926.04.d: In January Feng Yuxiang stepped down, and the Fengtian Army, the Zhili Army and the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army, together with the Shanxi Army, jointly attacked the Guominjun. On 12 March came the Dagukou Incident, and Japan joined with the Powers in issuing an ultimatum; on the 18th Beijing citizens petitioning the government were shot down by the guards of the Provisional Executive Government, resulting in the March 18 Massacre; on the 23rd the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army retook Tianjin, on 15 April the Guominjun withdrew from Beijing to hold Nankou, and Duan Qirui fled on the 20th. Wu Peifu regained Henan, and Liu Zhenhua entered Shaanxi and laid siege to Xi'an. On 20 March Chiang Kai-shek engineered the Zhongshan Warship Incident; Guangdong and Guangxi were unified, and the Southern Expedition army took Hainan; Tang Shengzhi drove out Zhao Hengti and entered Changsha. Meanwhile Ibn Saud proclaimed himself King of the Hejaz in January; in April communal clashes broke out in Calcutta, India.
1926.04.t: Guangdong and Guangxi unified · March 18 Massacre

1926.07.d: Driven forward by KMT–CPC cooperation, the National Revolutionary Army took its oath in Guangzhou on 9 July and set out on the Northern Expedition, with the aim of overthrowing the imperialist-backed Beiyang warlords; Tang Shengzhi's forces formed the vanguard, taking Changsha on the 11th and pressing towards the Miluo River. In the north the Fengtian, Zhili and Shanxi warlords joined forces to besiege the Guominjun, whose stubborn defence of Nankou had lasted over three months, while Liu Zhenhua's Zhensong Army besieged Xi'an; Sun Chuanfang, holding the five southeastern provinces and claiming to “keep the region secure and the people at peace”, sat back to watch the outcome in Hunan and Hubei. Tang Jiyao held Yunnan, and the Sichuan generals each ruled their own zones. In June the June Tenth Movement broke out in Korea on the occasion of Emperor Sunjong's state funeral; within the Soviet party the struggle between the United Opposition and Stalin came into the open.

1926.10.d: In late August the Northern Expedition Army took Tingsiqiao and Heshengqiao in quick succession, in September it took Hanyang and Hankou, and after besieging Wuchang for forty days it captured the city on 10 October, shattering Wu Peifu's main force. It then turned on Jiangxi and fought fiercely with Sun Chuanfang: Nanchang was taken and lost again and a second attack failed, while western and southern Jiangxi had been taken first, and the Eastern Route Army entered western Fujian. In the north the Guominjun withdrew from Nankou in August; Feng Yuxiang returned from the Soviet Union and on 17 September held the oath-taking at Wuyuan, renaming his forces the Guominjun Allied Army and joining the National Revolution. In October the All-Union Communist Party (Bolsheviks) expelled Trotsky from the Politburo.

1926.12.d: In early November the Northern Expedition Army took Jiujiang and Nanchang, destroying Sun Chuanfang's crack troops, and Jiangxi and Fujian passed to the National Revolutionary Army; on 28 November the Guominjun Allied Army lifted the siege of Xi'an, and the Guanzhong region passed to Feng Yuxiang. In half a year the Northern Expedition Army had fought its way from the Pearl River basin to the Yangtze basin. The Nationalist Government moved north and in December formed a Joint Council in Hankou, while Chiang Kai-shek held his headquarters at Nanchang; the dispute over moving the capital already foreshadowed the Nanjing–Wuhan split. The Sichuan and Guizhou armies one after another adopted revolutionary army designations; the Beiyang warlords made Zhang Zuolin commander-in-chief of the Anguojun. Emperor Taishō of Japan died on 25 December and the era name was changed to Shōwa; in November the Communist Party of Indonesia's uprising in Java failed.
1926.12.t: Southeast secured · Capital moved to Wuhan

1927.04.d: The Eastern Route Army entered Hangzhou in February; on 22 March the Third Armed Uprising of the Shanghai Workers triumphed and welcomed the Northern Expedition Army into the city; on the 24th Nanjing was taken, whereupon British and American warships shelled the city, perpetrating the Nanjing Incident. On 12 April Chiang Kai-shek staged a counter-revolutionary coup in Shanghai, in which large numbers of Communists and revolutionary masses were arrested and killed; on the 18th he set up a separate Nationalist Government in Nanjing in opposition to the Wuhan Nationalist Government, and Nanjing, Wuhan and Beijing stood as three rival powers. The Fengtian Army moved south into Henan to take over from Wu Peifu, and the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army held Xuzhou and Bengbu; on the 28th Li Dazhao was murdered by the Fengtian warlords. In March–April the Shōwa financial crisis broke out in Japan; Tanaka Giichi formed a cabinet in April and turned to a hard-line China policy.

1927.08.d: In May the Wuhan Nationalist Government continued the Northern Expedition, fighting bloody battles with the Fengtian Army at Shangcai and Linying, while Feng Yuxiang came out through Tong Pass and took Zhengzhou and Kaifeng; after the Xuzhou Conference in June he went over to Nanjing, and Henan passed to the Second Army Group; Yan Xishan changed his flag, and Zhang Zuolin became Generalissimo of the Anguojun Military Government. On 15 July the Wang Jingwei clique carried out the “purge of Communists” in Wuhan, and the National Revolution failed. On 1 August the CPC launched the Nanchang Uprising, firing the first shot of armed resistance against the KMT reactionaries; on the 7th it held the August 7 Meeting. Chiang Kai-shek stepped down on the 13th; Sun Chuanfang seized the opportunity to cross the Yangtze, but after six days of fierce fighting at Longtan he was defeated and driven back. Japan first sent troops into Shandong in May, and held the Eastern Conference in June–July.

1927.10.d: The Nanjing and Wuhan governments merged and in September formed the Central Special Committee in Nanjing; Tang Shengzhi held Hunan and Hubei in defiance of its orders, and in late October Nanjing ordered the Western Expedition. The Nanchang Uprising forces moved south to Chaozhou and Shantou and were defeated at Tangkeng and Liusha in early October, the survivors following Zhu De into the Fujian-Jiangxi-Guangdong border area; the Autumn Harvest Uprising forces were checked in their attack on Changsha, and Mao Zedong led them towards the countryside; after the Sanwan Reorganization they reached Maoping in Ninggang on 7 October and began building the Jinggangshan Revolutionary Base Area. In the north war broke out between Shanxi and Fengtian; Fu Zuoyi seized Zhuozhou in a surprise attack, and the Fengtian Army besieged the city. Sukarno founded the Indonesian Nationalist Party in July; in October the Soviet Union expelled Trotsky and Zinoviev from the Central Committee of the All-Union Communist Party (Bolsheviks).
1927.10.t: Autumn Harvest Uprising · March to Jinggangshan

1927.12.d: The Western Expedition army fought its way into Wuhan in November; Tang Shengzhi fled to Japan, and Hubei came under the Wuhan Branch Political Council controlled by the New Guangxi Clique; the Northern Expedition Army retook Xuzhou on 16 December, securing northern Jiangsu and northern Anhui. In November soviet governments were set up in Haifeng and Lufeng, and the Huangma Uprising forces briefly took Huang'an; on 11 December Zhang Tailei and others led the Guangzhou Uprising and set up the Guangzhou Soviet Government, which held out for three days before failing, after which the Nanjing Nationalist Government broke off relations with the Soviet Union. In December Chiang Kai-shek married Soong Mei-ling and prepared to return to office. The 15th Congress of the All-Union Communist Party (Bolsheviks) expelled the Trotskyists; the Indian parties boycotted Britain's Simon Commission.

1928.05.d: Chiang Kai-shek returned to office, reorganized the forces into four army groups and resumed the Northern Expedition in April. The First Army Group entered Jinan on 1 May; to obstruct the Northern Expedition, Japan, on the pretext of protecting its nationals, sent troops into Shandong for the second time and on the 3rd perpetrated the Jinan Massacre, brutally killing the diplomatic commissioner Cai Gongshi; the Northern Expedition Army was forced to make a detour and cross the Yellow River northward; Feng Yuxiang's Second Army Group advanced into western Shandong and southern Hebei, and Yan Xishan's Third Army Group attacked north along the Beijing–Hankou Railway. After the Southern Hunan Uprising, Zhu De and Chen Yi led their forces to Jinggangshan in late April, joined forces with Mao Zedong's forces and formed the Fourth Army of the Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army (later called the Red Fourth Army). On 15 March Japan carried out mass arrests of Communists at home.

1928.06.d: Zhang Zuolin withdrew from Beijing on 3 June; on the 4th his special train was blown up by the Japanese Kwantung Army at Huanggutun, and he died of his wounds; Shanxi troops entered Beijing on the 8th, and the rule of the Beiyang warlords came to an end; Beijing was soon renamed Beiping. Zhang Xueliang kept his father's death secret, returned to Fengtian and took over the government, and the remnants of the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army fell back east of the Luan River. In Xinjiang, Yang Zengxin changed his flag on 1 July and was assassinated soon after, on the 7th. On 23 June the Red Fourth Army at Jinggangshan won a great victory at Longyuankou, and the armed independent regime of workers and peasants in the Hunan-Jiangxi border area entered its heyday. The Kwantung Army had intended to seize the Northeast amid the turmoil, but did not obtain Tokyo's approval.
1928.06.t: Huanggutun · Northern Expedition Army enters Beijing

1928.12.d: With the Northern Expedition completed, in October Nanjing adopted the five-yuan system and Chiang Kai-shek became Chairman of the Nationalist Government. Defying Japanese obstruction, Zhang Xueliang announced the Northeast Flag Replacement by circular telegram on 29 December, and the Nanjing Nationalist Government nominally unified the country; yet the army groups each occupied a region of their own: the Shanxi Clique held Beiping, Tianjin, Hebei, Chahar and Suiyuan, Feng Yuxiang held Henan, Shaanxi and Gansu, the Guangxi Clique controlled Hunan, Hubei and eastern Hebei, and Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou and Xinjiang remained a law unto themselves. After the Pingjiang Uprising Peng Dehuai led the Red Fifth Army up to Jinggangshan; the Red Army forces and base areas on the Xin River and the Hubei-Henan border gradually grew. In November Japan held the enthronement ceremony of Emperor Shōwa; in Afghanistan a revolt against the reforms broke out.

1929.04.d: In January the Disbandment Conference broke up in discord, and wars among the new warlords followed: in February came the Hunan Incident, in March Nanjing launched a punitive campaign against the Guangxi Clique, and on 5 April Chiang Kai-shek's Central Army entered Wuhan; Li Mingrui changed sides and the Guangxi Clique collapsed without a fight; Li Jishen was detained at Tangshan, Chen Jitang took charge of Guangdong, and Tang Shengzhi regained his former troops in eastern Hebei. In January the Red Fourth Army left Jinggangshan and marched into southern Jiangxi; the battle at Dabaidi turned its passive position around, and in March it took Changting for the first time and fought its way across southern Jiangxi and western Fujian. In March China and Japan agreed on the withdrawal of Japanese troops from Jinan. King Amanullah of Afghanistan abdicated in January, and Kabul fell into the hands of Bacha-i Saqao.
1929.04.t: Chiang–Guangxi War · Red Army descends on southern Jiangxi

1929.11.d: In May Han Fuju and Shi Yousan defected to Chiang, and Feng Yuxiang pulled his troops back west of Tong Pass; in October Song Zheyuan and others issued a circular telegram against Chiang, the Chiang–Feng War raged in western Henan, and the Northwestern Army was defeated and fell back in November. Zhang Fakui rose against Chiang at Yichang and moved south, forming the Zhang Fakui–Guangxi Allied Army with the Guangxi Clique, which had returned to Guangxi. In July the northeastern authorities took back the Chinese Eastern Railway by force, provoking the Chinese Eastern Railway Incident; in October–November Soviet troops attacked Tongjiang, Jalainur and Manzhouli, and the Northeastern Army was defeated. The Red Fourth Army opened up a revolutionary base area in western Fujian. In October the New York stock market crashed, and the economic crisis of the capitalist world broke out and spread to Asia; in November the Gwangju Student Movement broke out in Korea.
1929.11.t: Chinese Eastern Railway Incident · Chiang–Feng War

1930.07.d: Yan Xishan, Feng Yuxiang and Li Zongren joined forces against Chiang, and in May the Central Plains War broke out in full, with a million troops locked in fierce fighting along the Longhai, Beiping–Hankou and Tianjin–Pukou railways; the Shanxi Army entered Jinan in June, and on 13 July Wang Jingwei and others convened the Enlarged Conference in Beiping. The Guangxi–Zhang Fakui Army marched north and took Changsha and Yueyang, but was defeated by the Guangdong Army at Hengyang in June; the Yunnan Army was ordered to besiege Nanning. The Gutian Meeting of the Red Fourth Army in December 1929 had established the principles of building the Party ideologically and the army politically. Under the guidance of Li Lisan's “Left” errors, the Red Third Army Group broke into Changsha on 27 July and withdrew on 6 August. In India Gandhi led the Salt March in March–April; in Vietnam the Yên Bái Uprising broke out in February and the Communist Party of Vietnam was founded.
1930.07.t: Central Plains War · Red Army attacks Changsha

1930.12.d: In September the Beiping Nationalist Government was set up with Yan Xishan as Chairman; on the 18th Zhang Xueliang declared his support for Nanjing by circular telegram, and the Northeastern Army entered North China and took over Beiping, Tianjin, Hebei and Chahar; Yan and Feng stepped down in November, and the Central Plains War ended in victory for Chiang Kai-shek. Yang Hucheng took charge of Shaanxi, Han Fuju was moved to govern Shandong, and Britain returned Weihaiwei in October. The Red First Front Army took Ji'an in October; in December the KMT forces launched the first “encirclement” campaign against the Central Revolutionary Base Area, and the Red Army lured the enemy in deep, capturing the division commander Zhang Huizan alive at Longgang on the 30th. In October the Wushe Uprising, in which Gaoshan compatriots in Taiwan rose against Japan, broke out; Japanese Prime Minister Hamaguchi Osachi was shot by an assassin in November; in Burma the Saya San Rebellion broke out.
1930.12.t: Northeastern Army enters North China · Counter-“encirclement” campaigns

1931.07.d: In January the Red Army won again at Dongshao, breaking the first “encirclement”; in May, in the second counter-“encirclement” campaign, it swept 700 li in fifteen days, fighting from Futian to Jianning. In February Chiang Kai-shek placed Hu Hanmin under house arrest; Guangdong and Guangxi turned against Chiang and on 28 May set up a separate Nationalist Government in Guangzhou, and Nanjing and Guangzhou stood opposed; Shi Yousan, commissioned by Guangzhou, raised troops in southern Hebei. In July Chiang Kai-shek made himself commander-in-chief and launched the third “encirclement” campaign. The Tibetan army and the Sichuan-Xikang Army went to war over the Dargye–Beri dispute, and in February the Tibetan army seized Garze in a surprise attack; in Xinjiang the Hami Incident broke out, and Ma Zhongying entered Xinjiang. Japan engineered the Wanbaoshan Incident near Changchun and stirred up anti-Chinese massacres in Korea.

1931.11.d: On 18 September the Japanese Kwantung Army blew up a stretch of railway near Liutiaohu, falsely blamed it on Chinese troops and attacked Shenyang, perpetrating the September 18 Incident; the Northeastern Army was ordered not to resist, and within ten days the key places of Liaoning and Jilin provinces had fallen. The September 18 Incident was the starting point of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression. In November Ma Zhanshan fought the Japanese at the Nen River Bridge; Qiqihar fell on the 19th, while Jinzhou and Harbin remained in Chinese hands. In September the Red Army broke the third “encirclement”, and on 7 November the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic was established in Ruijin. Nanjing and Guangzhou held peace talks, and each convened its own Fourth National Congress. The League of Nations set a deadline for the withdrawal of Japanese troops, to no effect; in Japan the October Incident plot for a military coup was exposed.

1932.03.d: Japanese troops seized Jinzhou in January and took Harbin in February; on 1 March Japan installed Puyi at the head of Puppet Manchukuo in Changchun, renaming Changchun “Xinjing”; the Northeast Anti-Japanese Volunteer Armies of Li Du, Wang Delin and others still held eastern Jilin. On 28 January Japanese troops attacked Shanghai; the 19th Route Army and the Fifth Army rose to resist, and the January 28 Songhu Resistance lasted more than a month, until in early March the Chinese troops withdrew to the Jiading–Huangdu line and fighting stopped. The Red Army besieged Ganzhou for over a month without taking it. The Nanjing Nationalist Government, the Southwest Political Council in Guangzhou and the regional power-holders were united in name but divided in fact. Meanwhile in Japan the League of Blood carried out a series of assassinations, and party cabinets were nearing their end.

1932.12.d: The Northeast Anti-Japanese Volunteer Armies suffered one defeat after another; Ma Zhanshan and Su Bingwen withdrew into the Soviet Union, and Japanese and puppet troops advanced to the eastern and western ends of the Chinese Eastern Railway. The fourth counter-“encirclement” campaigns in the Hubei-Henan-Anhui and Western Hunan-Hubei areas failed; the Red Fourth Front Army crossed the Qinling and Daba Mountains westward and in December entered Tongjiang in northern Sichuan; He Long led the Red Third Army back to the Hunan-Hubei border after a long fighting march. In the autumn the Red Army of the Central Soviet Area moved east and took Jianning, Lichuan and Taining. In Sichuan the War of the Two Lius broke out, and Han Fuju drove Liu Zhennian out of Jiaodong. The League of Nations' Lytton Commission published its report in October. Meanwhile the May 15 Incident took place in Japan, and Inukai Tsuyoshi was assassinated.
1932.12.t: Red Fourth Front Army enters Sichuan

1933.05.d: Japanese troops took Shanhaiguan in January and overran Rehe in ten days in February–March, Tang Yulin abandoning Chengde. Chinese troops resisted at the passes of the Great Wall for two months; in May the Japanese crossed the Great Wall and closed in on Beiping and Tianjin, and on the 31st the Tanggu Truce was signed, which in effect recognized Japan's occupation of the Northeast and Rehe and made eastern Hebei a demilitarized zone. Feng Yuxiang cooperated with the CPC and on 26 May formed the Anti-Japanese Allied Army in Zhangjiakou. In the fourth counter-“encirclement” campaign the Central Soviet Area won great victories at Huangpi and Caotaigang; the Red Fourth Front Army established the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area around Tongjiang, Nanjiang and Bazhong. In Xinjiang, Sheng Shicai came to power through the “April 12” coup, and separatist forces in Hotan and elsewhere in southern Xinjiang rebelled. Meanwhile Japan withdrew from the League of Nations in March.

1933.11.d: The Anti-Japanese Allied Army recovered Duolun in July, but soon, caught between Japanese and KMT forces, it was defeated in August. After the officer training at Mount Lu, Chiang Kai-shek advanced behind lines of blockhouses and launched the fifth “encirclement” campaign against the Central Revolutionary Base Area; Lichuan was lost in September. On 20 November the 19th Route Army and Li Jishen set up the People's Revolutionary Government of the Chinese Republic in Fuzhou, having already concluded a preliminary agreement with the Red Army. The Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area won victory after victory, expanding to Xuanhan and Daxian, and Liu Xiang was ordered to attack it along six routes; Liu Wenhui, defeated in the War of the Two Lius, fell back to Ya'an. In November the separatist forces of southern Xinjiang set up the so-called “Islamic Republic of East Turkestan” in Kashi. Meanwhile King Nadir Shah of Afghanistan was assassinated (November).

1934.04.d: The Central Army entered Fujian in January, the Fujian People's Government failed, and the 19th Route Army was reorganized. On 1 March Puyi proclaimed himself emperor in Changchun, and Puppet Manchukuo was renamed the “Empire of Manchukuo”. Under the command of Bo Gu and Otto Braun, the Red Army slugged it out at Guangchang for eighteen days with “short, swift thrusts”; on 28 April Guangchang was lost, and the northern gate of the Central Soviet Area lay wide open. Ma Zhongying again besieged Dihua; Soviet troops entered Xinjiang to help Sheng Shicai lift the siege, and Ma's forces moved south and took Kashi, while the “East Turkestan” separatist regime fell back to Hotan. Prince De's Mongolian Local Autonomy Political Council was established at Bailingmiao; the 13th Dalai Lama had died in December of the previous year, and Reting became regent. Chiang Kai-shek launched the New Life Movement in Nanchang. Meanwhile Japan issued the “Amō Statement”, claiming exclusive domination over China.
1934.04.t: Battle of Guangchang · Puppet Manchukuo becomes a monarchy

1934.10.d: Owing to the “Left” errors in the leadership, the fifth counter-“encirclement” campaign failed; from 10 October the 86,000 men of the Central Red Army were forced to withdraw from the Central Revolutionary Base Area, setting out from Ruijin and Yudu on the Long March, and in the latter part of the month they broke through the first blockade line between Xinfeng and Anyuan; Xiang Ying, Chen Yi and others stayed behind with their forces to carry on guerrilla warfare in the south. The Red Sixth Army Group had set out on its Western March in August, and on 24 October joined forces with He Long's Red Third Army at Muhuang in eastern Guizhou. The Red 25th Army was still holding out in Hubei-Henan-Anhui. In Xinjiang, Ma Zhongying went into the Soviet Union in July and Ma Hushan held Hotan; Hexi passed to Ma Bufang and Ma Buqing. Meanwhile the Okada cabinet was formed in Japan (July).
1934.10.t: Long March of the Central Red Army

1934.12.d: The Central Red Army broke through three blockade lines in succession, and from late November to 1 December fought a bloody battle on the Xiang River between Quanzhou and Xing'an, breaking through the fourth blockade line, but losing more than half of its 80,000-odd men; in December, with the change of course at Tongdao and the Liping Meeting, it abandoned the plan to head for western Hunan and turned instead towards Guizhou, where the KMT forces were weak, reaching Houchang on the south bank of the Wu River at the end of the month. Ruijin was occupied by KMT forces on 10 November, and only guerrilla zones remained of the Central Soviet Area. The Red Second and Sixth Army Groups created the Hunan-Hubei-Sichuan-Guizhou Base Area at Yongshun and Dayong in western Hunan; the Red 25th Army set out on its Long March into southern Shaanxi and created the Hubei-Henan-Shaanxi Base Area. Meanwhile Japan announced its abrogation of the Washington Naval Treaty.
1934.12.t: Battle of the Xiang River · Change of course at Tongdao

1935.01.d: In early January the Central Red Army forced its way across the Wu River and took Zunyi on the 7th; on 15–17 January it held the Zunyi Meeting, which in effect established Mao Zedong's leading position in the Party Central Committee and the Red Army, a turning point of life-and-death importance in the history of the Party; on the 19th it moved north, suffered a setback in the Battle of Tucheng on the 28th, and on the 29th made the first crossing of the Chishui River into southern Sichuan. Xue Yue led the KMT Central Army in pursuit into Guiyang, and Guizhou began to come under the control of the Nanjing central government. The Red Fourth Front Army launched the Guangyuan–Zhaohua Campaign, and the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area still held; Fang Zhimin, leading the Red Tenth Army Group (the Northward Anti-Japanese Vanguard), was defeated and captured in the Huaiyu Mountains. Meanwhile Japanese and puppet troops clashed with Outer Mongolian troops on the border at Halhamiao.

1935.03.d: In February the Central Red Army reorganized at Zhaxi, made the second crossing of the Chishui River back into northern Guizhou, won great victories at Loushan Pass and Zunyi and occupied Zunyi again; in March it made the third and fourth crossings of the Chishui, at the end of the month crossed the Wu River southward and feinted towards Guiyang, and under Mao Zedong's command broke out of the encirclement by KMT forces several hundred thousand strong. At the end of March the Red Fourth Front Army forced its way across the Jialing River. The Red Second and Sixth Army Groups fought counter-“encirclement” battles in Hunan-Hubei-Sichuan-Guizhou, and the Red 25th Army held out in southern Shaanxi. The Sichuan provincial government moved to Chengdu, and Liu Xiang unified the administration of Sichuan. Meanwhile the Soviet Union sold the Chinese Eastern Railway to Puppet Manchukuo (March).
1935.03.t: Four crossings of the Chishui River

1935.05.d: Feinting towards Kunming, the Central Red Army skilfully crossed the Jinsha River at Jiaopingdu in early May; after the Huili Meeting it passed through the Yi areas, where the Yihai Alliance was concluded; on the night of the 24th it took Anshunchang and on the 25th forced a crossing of the Dadu River, and on the 29th it seized Luding Bridge in a lightning strike. The Red Fourth Front Army left the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area and moved west to hold the area around Maoxian, Lixian and Beichuan. Wang Jialie was forced from office, and Guizhou came under the Nanjing central government. Using the Hebei Incident as a pretext, Japan extended its aggression in North China. Meanwhile the Philippine Commonwealth constitution was approved by plebiscite, and the Quetta earthquake struck British India (31 May).
1935.05.t: Crossing the Jinsha River · Seizure of Luding Bridge

1935.06.d: On 12 June the Central Red Army crossed Jiajin Mountain and joined forces with the Red Fourth Front Army at Dawei and Maogong; on the 26th the Lianghekou Meeting decided on the policy of going north. The Red Army in northern Shaanxi, in its second counter-“encirclement” campaign, took Anding, Ansai, Bao'an, Jingbian and other counties in succession, linking the two base areas of Shaanxi and Gansu into one. The Nationalist Government compromised with Japan: the He–Umezu Agreement forced Yu Xuezhong's forces and the Central Army out of Hebei, and the Qin–Doihara Agreement forced Song Zheyuan out of Chahar. Qu Qiubai died a heroic martyr's death in Changting. Meanwhile the struggle between the Control Faction and the Imperial Way Faction within the Japanese army reached fever pitch.

1935.09.d: The Red First and Fourth Front Armies went north in Left and Right Columns; the Right Column crossed the grasslands in August and won a great victory at Baozuo; Zhang Guotao refused to carry out the policy of going north and plotted to harm the Party Central Committee, and on 10 September the Central Committee led the Red First and Third Army Groups north on their own; at the Ejie Meeting these were reorganized as the Shaanxi-Gansu Detachment, which seized Lazikou on the 17th and reached Hadapu on the 20th. The Red 25th Army reached Yongping in northern Shaanxi in September and merged with the northern Shaanxi Red Army to form the Red 15th Army Group. Chiang Kai-shek transferred the Northeastern Army to northern Shaanxi to “suppress the Communists”. Song Zheyuan became Beiping–Tianjin Garrison Commander. Meanwhile the Seventh Congress of the Communist International was held, and the CPC issued the August 1 Declaration, calling for an end to the civil war and unity in resisting Japan.

1935.10.d: The Shaanxi-Gansu Detachment crossed the Liupan Mountains and on 19 October reached Wuqizhen in northern Shaanxi, and the Long March of the Central Red Army ended in victory; the Red 15th Army Group won victories at Laoshan and Yulinqiao. At Zhuomudiao Zhang Guotao set up a separate “Central Committee”, taking the road of splitting the Party and the Red Army, and the Red Fourth Front Army went south and launched the Sui-Chong-Dan-Mao Campaign. The Red Second and Sixth Army Groups were still in Hunan-Hubei-Sichuan-Guizhou. Japanese imperialism engineered the “autonomy of the five provinces of North China”. Meanwhile Italy invaded Ethiopia, and the League of Nations' sanctions proved ineffective.

1935.12.d: Japan engineered the North China Incident: Yin Rugeng set up the Puppet East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Government at Tongzhou, Nanjing set up the Hebei-Chahar Political Council headed by Song Zheyuan, and Li Shouxin's puppet Mongol troops occupied six counties of northern Chahar. On 9 December Beiping students marched to resist Japan and save the nation, and the December 9 Movement set off a new upsurge of the nationwide movement to resist Japan and save the nation. The Battle of Zhiluo (November) broke the third “encirclement”; the CPC Central Committee was based at Wayaobu, and in December the Wayaobu Meeting laid down the strategy of the Anti-Japanese National United Front. The Red Fourth Front Army suffered a setback at Baizhangguan but still held Tianquan; the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups set out on the Long March in November. The fabi currency reform was carried out. Meanwhile the Commonwealth of the Philippines was established, with Quezon inaugurated as President (November).

1936.05.d: From February to May the Red First Front Army, under the name of the Anti-Japanese Vanguard Army, made its Eastern Expedition into Shanxi, in which Liu Zhidan gave his life; it returned in May and soon launched its Western Expedition. The Red Second and Sixth Army Groups fought their way through the Wumeng Mountains, crossed the Jinsha River at Shigu in April and reached Zhongdian; the Red Fourth Front Army held Garze and Luhuo. With the backing of the Kwantung Army, Prince De set up the Puppet Mongol Military Government at Dehua on 12 May. The anti-Japanese armed forces in the Northeast were united into the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army. Meanwhile after the February 26 Incident the Hirota cabinet was formed in Japan, and the North China Garrison Army was reinforced; Zhang Xueliang made secret contact with the CPC in Xi'an.
1936.05.t: Red Army's Eastern Expedition · Red Second and Sixth Army Groups march north

1936.07.d: Chen Jitang, Li Zongren and Bai Chongxi raised troops against Chiang in the name of “going north to resist Japan” (the Guangdong–Guangxi Incident); the Guangdong air force and Yu Hanmou went over to Nanjing one after another, Chen Jitang stepped down on 18 July, and Guangdong came under the Nanjing central government; Guangxi made peace with Nanjing in September. The Red Army's Western Expedition took Dingbian, Yanchi and Yuwang; Wayaobu was lost, and the CPC Central Committee moved to Bao'an. On 2 July the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups joined forces with the Red Fourth Front Army at Garze and formed the Red Second Front Army, and early in the month they set off north together. Meanwhile the Spanish Civil War broke out.

1936.10.d: The Red Second and Fourth Front Armies went north into southern Gansu, and in August–September the Red Fourth Front Army launched the Min-Tao-Xi Campaign; on 9 October the Red First and Fourth Front Armies joined forces at Huining, and on the 22nd the Red First and Second Front Armies joined forces at Jiangtaibao; the three main forces were united and the Long March of the Red Army ended in victory, a great feat in human history. The plan for the Ningxia Campaign was thwarted; three armies of the Red Fourth Front Army crossed the Yellow River westward and by the end of the month held Yitiaoshan. With the Guangxi affair settled, the provincial capital moved back to Guilin. Japan pressed ever harder in the Kawagoe–Zhang Qun negotiations. Meanwhile Germany and Italy formed the Berlin–Rome Axis (October).
1936.10.t: Huining rendezvous · Victory of the Long March

1936.12.d: Fu Zuoyi's forces recovered Bailingmiao (24 November), and the Suiyuan War of Resistance inspired the whole nation; the Red Army won the Battle of Shanchengbao (21 November), forcing Hu Zongnan's forces to halt their pursuit. The Western Route Army fought hard at Gulang and held Yongchang and Shandan. On 12 December Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng, to compel Chiang to resist Japan, staged a military remonstrance and detained Chiang Kai-shek, an event known to history as the Xi'an Incident; the CPC Central Committee advocated a peaceful settlement and sent Zhou Enlai and others to Xi'an to negotiate; Chiang Kai-shek was forced to accept the proposals to stop the civil war and unite with the Communists to resist Japan, and was released on the 25th. The peaceful settlement of the Xi'an Incident became the pivot on which the situation turned. The Red Army took over the defence of Yan'an. Meanwhile Japan and Germany signed the Anti-Comintern Pact.
1936.12.t: Peaceful settlement of the Xi'an Incident

1937.07.d: From January to March the Western Route Army fought bloody battles at Gaotai and Nijiayingzi and was defeated. The Northeastern Army was transferred east to Henan and Anhui, and Yang Hucheng was forced to go abroad; the CPC Central Committee moved into Yan'an, and the KMT and CPC negotiated the reorganization of the Red Army. On 7 July Japanese troops engineered the Lugou Bridge Incident, and the Chinese defenders rose to resist; the Lugou Bridge Incident marked the beginning of the nationwide War of Resistance; on the 17th Chiang Kai-shek delivered his Lushan Talk; Beiping fell on the 29th and Tianjin on the 30th, and Song Zheyuan fell back to Baoding. In southern Xinjiang the forces of Mahmud Muhiti and Ma Hushan rebelled. Meanwhile the Konoe cabinet was formed in Japan and announced the dispatch of troops to North China.
1937.07.t: Lugou Bridge Incident · Nationwide War of Resistance

1937.09.d: The nationwide War of Resistance unfolded. The Battle of Songhu was at its height, with Chinese troops locked in fierce fighting with the Japanese along the Luodian–Dachang line in the northern outskirts of Shanghai; in North China the Japanese advanced along the Beiping–Hankou, Tianjin–Pukou and Beiping–Suiyuan railways, Datong fell on 13 September and Baoding and Cangzhou on 24 September, and the Puppet South Chahar Autonomous Government was set up in Zhangjiakou. On 25 September the 115th Division of the Eighth Route Army won the Pingxingguan Victory. The Declaration on KMT–CPC Cooperation was published, and the Anti-Japanese National United Front was formally established; the Red Army was reorganized as the Eighth Route Army, and the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region Government was set up. Asia: in August China and the Soviet Union signed a non-aggression treaty, and the Soviet Union began to aid China; the Soviet Union forcibly deported the Koreans of the Far East to Central Asia.

1937.11.d: Large tracts of North and East China fell. Niangzi Pass was lost in late October, the defenders of Xinkou were forced to pull back, Taiyuan fell on 8 November, and the Shanxi provincial government withdrew to Linfen; the Eighth Route Army pushed deep behind enemy lines and opened up the battlefield behind enemy lines; the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Military Region was set up at Wutai, and the 120th Division entered northwestern Shanxi. Chinese troops fought a bloody battle in Shanghai for three months and withdrew on 12 November, while the Japanese, having landed at Hangzhou Bay, drove deep into southern Jiangsu. On 20 November the Nationalist Government announced its move to Chongqing. At Guisui the Japanese installed the Puppet Mongol United Autonomous Government, which together with the Puppet South Chahar and Puppet North Shanxi regimes formed the Puppet Mengjiang United Committee. Asia: Japan set up a wartime Imperial General Headquarters; Italy joined the Japanese-German Anti-Comintern Pact.

1937.12.d: Nanjing fell on 13 December, and the Japanese invading troops perpetrated the appalling Nanjing Massacre, in which more than 300,000 compatriots were killed within six weeks; Hangzhou, Wuhu and Yangzhou fell one after another, all the gateways to the lower Yangtze were lost, and the Supreme Command and most government organs moved temporarily to Wuhan. In North China the Japanese crossed the Yellow River and invaded southward; Han Fuju abandoned his defences, and Jinan fell on 27 December. In Beiping the Japanese installed Wang Kemin to organize the Puppet North China Provisional Government. The 9th Panchen Lama died at Yushu on 1 December. Asia: Japanese aircraft sank the US gunboat Panay, and Britain and the United States protested but did not intervene; in Japan, government and public opinion began to call for “not dealing with the Nationalist Government”.

1938.04.d: The Battle of Xuzhou unfolded. The Japanese advanced from north and south along the Tianjin–Pukou Railway; Bengbu was lost in February and Tengxian in March, where Wang Mingzhang died for his country; Li Zongren commanded the Battle of Tai'erzhuang and routed the Japanese on 7 April, winning the Tai'erzhuang Victory, the greatest victory on the frontal battlefield since the war began. In North China the Japanese occupied Linfen and Yuncheng; the Eighth Route Army smashed the Japanese “nine-route converging attack” in southeastern Shanxi, and the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei, Shanxi-Hebei-Henan and Southern Hebei Anti-Japanese Base Areas took initial shape. On 28 March Liang Hongzhi's Puppet Reformed Government was set up in Nanjing. The KMT's Provisional National Congress in Wuchang adopted the Programme of Armed Resistance and National Reconstruction. Asia: in January the Konoe Statement declared that Japan would “not deal with the Nationalist Government”; in April Japan promulgated the National Mobilization Law.

1938.06.d: The Japanese closed in on Xuzhou from all sides; Xuzhou fell on 19 May, and the main Chinese forces broke out by separate routes; the Battle of Lanfeng in eastern Henan was lost, and Kaifeng fell on 6 June. On 9 June KMT forces breached the Yellow River dyke at Huayuankou near Zhengzhou, holding up the Japanese for several months but creating the Yellow River flooded area across Henan, Anhui and Jiangsu, where hundreds of thousands of people died and more than ten million were affected. Xiamen was lost in May. The Japanese pushed west up the Yangtze, Anqing fell on 12 June, and the Battle of Wuhan began; the Advance Detachment of the New Fourth Army thrust behind enemy lines to Maoshan in southern Jiangsu. Asia: Japan reshuffled the Konoe cabinet, and Ugaki Kazushige, as Foreign Minister, sounded out the possibility of peace talks; Britain's naval base at Singapore was completed early in the year.
1938.06.t: Fall of Xuzhou · Huayuankou dyke breach

1938.10.d: The Battle of Wuhan lasted four and a half months: the Japanese advanced along both banks of the Yangtze and the northern foot of the Dabie Mountains, Jiujiang and Xinyang were lost in turn, and Xue Yue directed Chinese troops in encircling and wiping out most of the Japanese 106th Division at Wanjialing; the Japanese landed at Daya Bay on 12 October and occupied Guangzhou on the 21st, and Wuhan was lost on 25–27 October; the War of Resistance entered the stage of strategic stalemate. All Nationalist Government organs moved to Chongqing, and the great evacuation was organized at Yichang. The Sixth Plenary Session of the Sixth CPC Central Committee was held in Yan'an, and the headquarters of the New Fourth Army was at Yunling in southern Anhui. Asia: in July–August Soviet and Japanese troops fought at Zhanggufeng at the mouth of the Tumen River, and the Japanese were defeated and fell back; Japan then put forward the “New Order in East Asia”.

1939.03.d: With the stage of stalemate beginning, Japan's policy towards the Nationalist Government turned mainly to political inducements to capitulate. The Japanese occupied Yueyang in November, and Changsha was consumed by the Wenxi Fire; the Nanyue Military Conference laid down the guidelines for the second phase of the War of Resistance. In December Wang Jingwei fled to Hanoi and issued the Yan Telegram in response to the Konoe Statement, openly going over to the enemy. The Burma Road opened to traffic, and Xikang became a province in January 1939; the Fifth Plenary Session of the Fifth KMT Central Executive Committee adopted the policy of “dissolving, guarding against and restricting the Communists”. The Japanese invaded Hainan Island in February and took Nanchang on 27 March. In North China the Japanese carried out repeated “mopping-up” operations, and the main force of the 115th Division of the Eighth Route Army entered Shandong. Asia: the Hiranuma cabinet came to power in Japan; Soviet–Japanese clashes on the border between Puppet Manchukuo and Mongolia were growing.
1939.03.t: Battle of Nanchang · Fall of Hainan

1939.09.d: In May Japanese aircraft carried out the May 3–4 air raids on Chongqing. In the Battle of Suixian–Zaoyang the Japanese were checked and withdrew; in June the Japanese occupied Shantou and Dinghai and blockaded the British and French concessions in Tianjin, and Britain compromised and gave way. In July the Japanese took Changzhi and other towns in southeastern Shanxi. On 1 September the Japanese set up the Puppet Mengjiang United Autonomous Government in Zhangjiakou. In mid-September the Japanese attacked Changsha along three routes, and Xue Yue directed Chinese troops in blocking them at every step. The Eighth Route Army wiped out Japanese forces at Qihui in central Hebei, at Chenzhuang in Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei and at Liangshan in western Shandong. Asia: in May–September the Soviet Union and Japan fought the Battle of Nomonhan, in which the Japanese suffered a heavy defeat; in August came the Soviet–German treaty, and in September war broke out in Europe, Japan declaring that it would not intervene.

1939.12.d: In the First Battle of Changsha the Japanese withdrew in early October; the Eighth Route Army killed the Japanese Lieutenant General Abe Norihide at Huangtuling near Laiyuan. In November the Japanese landed at Qinzhou Bay and took Nanning on the 24th, cutting the international route between Guangxi and Vietnam; Du Yuming's Fifth Army recovered Kunlun Pass at the end of December. The Nationalist Government launched the Winter Offensive, with all war zones attacking at once. The KMT diehards stirred up the first anti-Communist upsurge: after the Zhugou Incident, Yan Xishan launched the Western Shanxi Incident, in which his old army attacked the Shanxi New Army. Asia: the US–Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation, whose abrogation the United States had announced, was about to lapse; Britain and France were pulling back in the Far East to deal with the war in Europe.
1939.12.t: Battle of Southern Guangxi · Winter Offensive

1940.03.d: On 30 March Wang Jingwei established the Wang Jingwei Puppet Nationalist Government in Nanjing; the Puppet Reformed Government was merged into it, and the Puppet Provisional Government in Beiping was renamed the Puppet North China Political Council. After the Western Shanxi Incident, northwestern Shanxi passed to the Eighth Route Army and the New Army, and Yan Xishan fell back to southwestern Shanxi; in the Ci-Wu-She-Lin Campaign the Eighth Route Army struck back in self-defence and routed Zhu Huaibing's forces, and agreed garrison boundaries with the KMT forces in the Taihang Mountains and southern Hebei; the first anti-Communist upsurge was beaten back. Fu Zuoyi recovered Wuyuan in March. Yang Jingyu of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army died a hero's death for his country in February. Asia: the Yonai cabinet came to power in Japan, its “peace work” towards China proceeding in step with the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime; Britain expanded its forces and prepared for war in Burma and India.

1940.06.d: The Battle of Zaoyang–Yichang: in May the Japanese first attacked Zaoyang, then crossed the Han River westward to take Yichang; Zhang Zizhong, Commander-in-Chief of the 33rd Army Group, died a hero's death for his country at Nanguadian on 16 May; Yichang fell on 12 June, the Japanese pushed forward to the gateway of the Three Gorges, and Chongqing was bombed again and again by Japanese aircraft in “Operation 101”. The Puppet Guangdong Provincial Government was set up. In North China the Japanese pursued the “cage policy”, carving up the anti-Japanese base areas with railways, roads and blockhouses. Asia: France surrendered in June, and Japan pressed French Indochina and Britain to cut the routes carrying aid to China.
1940.06.t: Battle of Zaoyang–Yichang · Fall of Yichang

1940.09.d: From July Britain closed the Burma Road for three months, and the Vietnam route was also cut, leaving the northwest as China's only overland international link. On 20 August the Eighth Route Army launched the Hundred Regiments Campaign, raiding the Zhengding–Taiyuan, Datong–Puzhou, Beiping–Hankou and other railways and for a time capturing Niangzi Pass; it was the largest offensive campaign the Eighth Route Army had fought since the War of Resistance began. On 6 September the Nationalist Government formally designated Chongqing the auxiliary capital. The New Fourth Army's forces in northern Jiangsu advanced east to Huangqiao, while the forces of the KMT diehard Han Deqin waited for a chance to attack. Asia: in late September Japanese troops invaded Lạng Sơn in Vietnam from southern Guangxi via Zhennan Pass and moved into northern Vietnam, and on the 27th the Tripartite Pact of Japan, Germany and Italy was signed in Berlin.
1940.09.t: Hundred Regiments Campaign · Japan invades Vietnam

1941.01.d: In January the KMT diehards engineered the Southern Anhui Incident: as it moved north, the headquarters of the New Fourth Army was surrounded and attacked by KMT forces at Maolin in Jingxian; Ye Ting was detained and Xiang Ying was killed, and the second anti-Communist upsurge reached its peak; the Central Military Commission of the CPC promptly rebuilt the army headquarters in Yancheng, with Chen Yi as acting commander, and KMT–CPC cooperation did not break down. The Japanese controlled the large cities and railways of North, Central and South China, and the occupied areas were divided among the Puppet North China Political Council, the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime, Puppet Mengjiang and Puppet Manchukuo; outside the cities lay the anti-Japanese base areas of the Eighth Route Army and the New Fourth Army and the guerrilla zones of the KMT forces, while the Southwest and Northwest formed the Great Rear Area. Meanwhile Japanese troops had already moved into northern Vietnam, and Japan mediated in the Franco-Thai border war.

1941.07.d: In March the Japanese suffered a setback in the Battle of Shanggao; in April they landed in eastern Zhejiang and at the mouth of the Min River, and Ningbo, Shaoxing and Fuzhou fell; in May the KMT forces suffered a crushing defeat in the Battle of the Zhongtiao Mountains, and southern Shanxi was lost. In February Li Changjiang of Taizhou went over to the enemy with his troops; in July Japanese and puppet troops launched a large-scale “mopping-up” of Yancheng-Funing, and the headquarters of the New Fourth Army moved; the Fourth Division of the New Fourth Army withdrew from Henan-Anhui-Jiangsu. Faced with Japanese “mopping-up” and the KMT blockade, Yan'an launched the Great Production Movement, and the 359th Brigade reclaimed land and farmed at Nanniwan. Meanwhile in April the Soviet–Japanese Neutrality Pact was signed, in June Germany attacked the Soviet Union, and in July Japanese troops moved into southern Vietnam; the United States froze Japanese assets and soon afterwards embargoed oil to Japan.

1941.12.d: In the Second Battle of Changsha in September the Japanese briefly broke into Changsha before withdrawing; in October the Japanese crossed the Yellow River and occupied Zhengzhou, withdrawing to the north bank at the end of the month. The Japanese carried out a great autumn “mopping-up” of the anti-Japanese base areas in North China and pursued the “Three Alls Policy”; the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain, the Defence of Huangyadong and the breakout at Daqingshan in Yimeng all date from this time. On 8 December Japan launched a surprise attack on Pearl Harbor and the Pacific War broke out; Japanese troops moved into the Shanghai International Settlement, and the Hong Kong garrison surrendered on the 25th; the Nationalist Government formally declared war on Japan, Germany and Italy, and the Third Battle of Changsha began soon after. Meanwhile Japanese troops landed in Malaya and the Philippines, and Guam and Wake Island fell.

1942.02.d: In January the Japanese retreated in defeat from the Third Battle of Changsha, one of the few Allied victories in the early Pacific War. Twenty-six countries, among them China, the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union, signed the Declaration by United Nations, and the world anti-fascist alliance was formally established; Chiang Kai-shek became Supreme Commander of the China Theatre, and Stilwell was ordered to China. The CPC-led Dongjiang guerrillas secretly brought more than 800 cultural figures stranded in Hong Kong back to the interior. In February the Yan'an Rectification Movement began, and the Chinese Expeditionary Force entered Burma to fight. Meanwhile the Japanese took Manila; on 15 February the British forces in Singapore surrendered, and the Dutch East Indies were in peril.

1942.05.d: After the American Doolittle Raid on Tokyo in April, the Japanese launched the Battle of Zhejiang–Jiangxi in mid-May, taking Jinhua and Lanxi at the end of the month. The Chinese Expeditionary Force was defeated in Burma, and the Japanese invaded northward along the Burma Road, taking Wanding, Mangshi, Longling and Tengchong in early May; Chinese troops blew up the Huitong Bridge and faced the Japanese across the Nu River; the Burma Road was cut, and supplies for China were switched to the Hump air route. The Japanese carried out the great May First “mopping-up” in central Hebei, and the plains anti-Japanese base area was turned almost entirely into guerrilla zones; in the Taihang counter-“mopping-up” campaign Zuo Quan, Deputy Chief of Staff of the Eighth Route Army, died for his country. Meanwhile the Japanese occupied most of Burma and the whole of the Philippines; the Battle of the Coral Sea was fought.
1942.05.t: Expeditionary Force enters Burma · Southeast Asia falls

1942.08.d: In the Battle of Zhejiang–Jiangxi the Japanese destroyed the airfields at Quzhou, Lishui and elsewhere, and withdrew in mid-August, keeping only the Jinhua–Lanxi area. A severe drought struck Henan, and famine spread. In Xinjiang, Sheng Shicai fell out with the Soviet Union; in August Soong Mei-ling flew to Dihua, and Xinjiang submitted to the Nationalist Government. In North China the Japanese pursued the “Public Security Strengthening Campaign”, digging blockade ditches and building blockhouses; the anti-Japanese base areas shrank in size and their population fell sharply, and they entered their most difficult period; the Eighth Route Army adopted the policy of better troops and simpler administration, and sent armed working teams deep into enemy-occupied areas. Meanwhile at the Battle of Midway in June the Japanese navy lost four aircraft carriers, and in August American forces landed on Guadalcanal.

1943.02.d: In January China signed new treaties with the United States and with Britain, abolishing extraterritoriality and other privileges in China; the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime declared war on Britain and the United States, and Japan announced the “return” of the concessions to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime. The Henan famine was at its worst; the KMT government went on levying grain for the army, and those who starved to death or fled the famine numbered in the millions. In February the Japanese seized Guangzhouwan, the French leased territory, and the Leizhou Peninsula, and also attacked Wang Jinzai's forces at Honghu, north of the Yangtze in central Hubei; in Shandong, Wu Huawen went over to the enemy with his troops, and Han Deqin's forces in northern Jiangsu were caught between Japanese and puppet troops. Meanwhile in February the Japanese withdrew from Guadalcanal, the German army surrendered at Stalingrad, and the Allies went over to the counter-offensive.

1943.11.d: In the Battle of Western Hubei in May the Japanese were checked before the Shipai fortress and fell back; the KMT diehards stirred up the third anti-Communist upsurge: in July Hu Zongnan moved troops in preparation for a lightning attack on the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region, but was forced to call it off after the CPC publicly exposed the plan. Han Deqin was defeated, and the Shandong-Jiangsu War Zone existed in name only; the Eighth Route Army's Taiyue forces moved south into the Zhongtiao Mountains, and the Eighth Route Army in Shandong routed Wu Huawen's puppet troops. Lin Sen died in August, and in October Chiang Kai-shek concurrently became Chairman of the Nationalist Government. In November the Battle of Changde was at its height, with Yu Chengwan's forces holding Changde to the last; the leaders of China, the United States and Britain held the Cairo Conference and agreed that the Northeast, Taiwan and Penghu would be returned to China. Meanwhile Italy surrendered, and US forces took Tarawa.

1944.05.d: In December Changde fell for a time and was then recovered, and the Dongjiang Column was formally established. In April 1944 the Japanese launched the Henan–Hunan–Guangxi Campaign (called “Operation Ichi-gō” by the Japanese), first opening up the southern section of the Beiping–Hankou Railway: in the Battle of Central Henan the KMT forces collapsed in headlong retreat, Zhengzhou and Xuchang fell in turn, and Luoyang was lost on 25 May, more than thirty cities having been lost in thirty-odd days; on the 27th the Japanese also attacked southward from Yueyang towards Changsha. On 11 May the Chinese Expeditionary Force forced its way across the Nu River, and the counter-offensive in western Yunnan began. Meanwhile Chinese and American troops took the Myitkyina airfield in a surprise attack, the Japanese Imphal offensive was checked, and US forces leapfrogged along New Guinea.

1944.08.d: The Battle of Changsha–Hengyang: Changsha fell on 18 June; Fang Xianjue's Tenth Army held Hengyang to the last for forty-seven days until the city fell on 8 August, and all the territory along the Xiang River was lost. In western Yunnan the Expeditionary Force besieged Songshan, Tengchong and Longling. In July the US Army Observation Group arrived in Yan'an, and the CPC and the Americans began direct contact. The battlefield behind enemy lines began partial counter-offensives: the New Fourth Army pushed west into Henan-Anhui-Jiangsu, and the Siming Mountains anti-Japanese base area in eastern Zhejiang expanded; the Communist Party of China became the mainstay of the nationwide War of Resistance. Meanwhile in June–August US forces took Saipan, Guam and Tinian, the Tōjō Hideki cabinet fell, and B-29s bombed the Japanese home islands from bases at Chengdu.

1944.12.d: The Japanese drove south along the Hunan–Guangxi Railway, taking Quanzhou and Wuzhou in September; Guilin and Liuzhou were lost around 10 November, and Nanning fell on the 24th; in early December their spearhead invaded Guizhou as far as Dushan before pulling back, and they linked up with the Japanese invading troops in Vietnam on the Sino-Vietnamese border, opening the continental communication line; Fuzhou and Wenzhou fell again. In the Henan–Hunan–Guangxi Campaign the KMT forces fell back in a great rout and lost vast tracts of territory. The Chinese Expeditionary Force in western Yunnan recovered Songshan and Tengchong in September and Longling and Mangshi in November. In September Sheng Shicai was transferred out, and in November the Yining Uprising broke out, beginning the Three Districts Revolution. In October Stilwell was recalled; Tannu Uriankhai was annexed by the Soviet Union. Meanwhile at the Battle of Leyte Gulf the main force of Japan's Combined Fleet was destroyed.
1944.12.t: Fall of Guilin and Liuzhou · Leyte Gulf

1945.03.d: In January the Japanese opened up the southern section of the Guangzhou–Hankou Railway, taking Qujiang and Chenzhou, and in February they took Ganzhou and other airfields in the southeast. On 20 January the Chinese Expeditionary Force recovered Wanding, western Yunnan was cleared of the enemy, and the China–India Road opened to traffic. Su Yu led part of the New Fourth Army south to form the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Military Region. In March the Japanese launched the Battle of Western Henan and Northern Hubei, attacking the Laohekou airfield. The CPC-led anti-Japanese base areas, taking advantage of the Japanese drawing off troops to the south, launched spring offensives.
