Meanwhile at the Yalta Conference in February the terms of Soviet entry into the war against Japan were secretly agreed behind China's back; US forces took Manila and Iwo Jima, Tokyo suffered the great air raid of 10 March, and British forces captured Mandalay.

1945.06.d: In April the Japanese took Laohekou; in the Battle of Western Hunan in April–June the Japanese attacked the Zhijiang airfield, were stopped in the Xuefeng Mountains and retreated in defeat. Chinese troops counter-attacked in Guangxi, recovering Nanning on 27 May and Liuzhou on 30 June; Fuzhou in May and Wenzhou in June were recovered in turn. The Seventh National Congress of the CPC was held in Yan'an and established Mao Zedong Thought as the Party's guiding ideology; the Sixth National Congress of the KMT was held in Chongqing; the two parties each made plans for the postwar period. The Eighth Route Army and the New Fourth Army took Funing and other towns, and the anti-Japanese base areas in central Hebei and western Henan expanded. Meanwhile Germany surrendered in May, British Indian forces recovered Rangoon, and in June US forces took Okinawa.

1945.08.d: On 28 July Chinese troops recovered Guilin. On 8 August the Soviet Union declared war on Japan, and the next day Soviet troops attacked into the Northeast, while Soviet–Mongolian forces entered northern Chahar and Rehe; on the 14th China and the Soviet Union signed the Treaty of Friendship and Alliance, and on the 15th Japan announced its unconditional surrender: the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression had been won. Puppet Manchukuo, the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime and Puppet Mengjiang collapsed one after another, and most Japanese troops inside the Great Wall waited where they were to surrender. The Eighth Route Army and the New Fourth Army launched a general counter-offensive and recovered Zhangjiakou on the 23rd; Yan Xishan returned to Taiyuan and Fu Zuoyi entered Guisui; on the 21st Japanese representatives came to Zhijiang to arrange the surrender, on the 28th Mao Zedong arrived in Chongqing, and on the 30th British forces returned to Hong Kong. Meanwhile the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Korea was divided at the 38th parallel into zones for accepting the Japanese surrender, the August Revolution took place in Vietnam, and Indonesia proclaimed its independence.

1945.10.d: The Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression had been won. With American airlift and sealift, the Nationalist Government rushed to take over Beiping, Tianjin, Shanghai, Nanjing and other large cities; the Japanese surrender was accepted in Taipei on 25 October, and Taiwan was restored. The people's army led by the CPC held the countryside of North and East China together with Zhangjiakou, Chengde, Yantai, Huaiyin and Handan, and advanced into the Northeast; Soviet troops occupied the Northeast. The Chongqing Negotiations produced the Double Tenth Agreement, while the army and people of the Liberated Areas had already struck back in self-defence in the Shangdang and Handan (Beiping–Hankou) Campaigns. Outer Mongolia held an independence referendum. Meanwhile Vietnam and Indonesia proclaimed independence, and British forces landed at Sài Gòn and on Java; Korea was occupied by the United States and the Soviet Union, divided along the 38th parallel.

1946.05.d: In January the ceasefire order and the Political Consultative Conference briefly raised hopes of peace, and the Nationalist Government recognized the independence of Outer Mongolia. Soviet troops withdrew from the Northeast in March–May, and the Northeast Democratic Allied Army moved into Harbin, Qiqihar and Changchun; the KMT forces advanced north along the Chinese Changchun Railway and, after the Defence of Siping, occupied Changchun and Jilin, halting at the Songhua River. In May the Nationalist Government returned to Nanjing. Marshall's mediation was still under way. Meanwhile the International Military Tribunal for the Far East opened, France and Vietnam signed the Agreement of 6 March, Soviet troops withdrew from Iran after the Iran crisis, and Transjordan became independent.

1946.12.d: In June the KMT forces launched a large-scale encirclement of the Central Plains Liberated Area, starting the full-scale civil war, and the War of Liberation began. The KMT forces occupied central and northern Jiangsu together with Huaiyin and Huai'an, Zhangjiakou, Chengde, Andong and Tonghua, while the army and people of the Liberated Areas won the Northern Suqian Campaign. In November the KMT unilaterally convened the National Assembly, which the CPC refused to attend, and Marshall's mediation headed for failure. In Xinjiang the Three Districts and the Nationalist Government formed a coalition provincial government. Meanwhile the Philippines became independent, the Netherlands and Indonesia signed the Linggadjati Agreement, and in December the Franco-Vietnamese war broke out in Hà Nội.

1947.03.d: The KMT forces switched from an all-out offensive to offensives against key areas, northern Shaanxi and Shandong: on 19 March Hu Zongnan's forces occupied Yan'an, and the CPC Central Committee withdrew of its own accord and fought on the move in northern Shaanxi; in Shandong the KMT forces occupied Linyi, and the East China Field Army wiped out Li Xianzhou's group at Laiwu. In Taiwan the February 28 Incident broke out on 28 February: the people rose against the autocratic rule of the KMT authorities, and KMT reinforcements were sent in to suppress them. The KMT–CPC peace talks broke down, and the CPC representatives left Nanjing. Meanwhile the Asian Relations Conference was held in New Delhi, and the Netherlands and Indonesia formally signed their agreement.
1947.03.t: February 28 Uprising · Fighting in northern Shaanxi

1947.08.d: After Menglianggu and Shajiadian, the KMT forces' offensives against key areas had been dealt heavy blows; at the end of June the Liu-Deng Army forced its way across the Yellow River, and in August it thrust into the Dabie Mountains; the Chen-Xie and Chen-Su forces moved south in turn, the People's Liberation Army went over to the strategic offensive, and the main battlefield shifted to the KMT-ruled areas north of the Yangtze. The KMT forces still held central Shandong and Yan'an in northern Shaanxi. The Northeast Democratic Allied Army's summer offensive liberated Andong and Tonghua. Meanwhile India and Pakistan were partitioned on 15 August, and millions of people migrated; the Netherlands launched its first “police action” against Indonesia.
1947.08.t: Thrust into the Dabie Mountains · Partition of India

1947.12.d: In November the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Field Army liberated Shijiazhuang, the first large city taken by the People's Liberation Army; Yuncheng and Qingjian were liberated, and the Chen-Xie Group thrust into western Henan. The KMT forces turned to attack Jiaodong and occupied Yantai and Weihai. After the autumn offensive in the Northeast the KMT forces pulled back along the Chinese Changchun and Beining Railways. Meanwhile the Kashmir war broke out, the United Nations adopted the resolution on the partition of Palestine, and Burma was about to become independent.

1948.06.d: The winter offensive in the Northeast liberated Siping, Jilin, Yingkou and Anshan, and the KMT forces were left besieged in the three cities of Changchun, Shenyang and Jinzhou; in the Northwest, after the great victory at Yichuan, Yan'an was recovered; Luoyang, Linfen and Weixian were liberated, and Kaifeng was liberated and then voluntarily relinquished. In April the KMT convened the “National Assembly under the Constitution”, which elected Chiang Kai-shek President; Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei and Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan were merged into the North China Liberated Area. Meanwhile Israel was founded and the First Middle East War broke out; Burma and Ceylon became independent, and a state of emergency was declared in Malaya.

1948.09.d: The East China Field Army liberated Jinan on 24 September, capturing its commander Wang Yaowu; the Central Shanxi Campaign liberated the outskirts of Taiyuan, and Xiangfan and Yanzhou were liberated. The North China People's Government was established. The KMT government issued the gold yuan notes, and prices in the KMT-ruled areas ran out of control. Meanwhile the Republic of Korea was established in the south and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea in the north; India sent troops into Hyderabad, and the Madiun Affair took place in Indonesia.

1948.11.d: The Liaoshen Campaign lasted 52 days: Jinzhou, Changchun and Shenyang were liberated one after another, and the whole of the Northeast was liberated; the Huaihai Campaign began on 6 November, Huang Baitao's army group was wiped out at Nianzhuang, and Huang Wei's army group was surrounded at Shuangduiji; Zhengzhou, Kaifeng, Chengde and Baoding were liberated, and the Pingjin Campaign had begun. Meanwhile the Tokyo Trial handed down its verdicts, the Dutch–Indonesian negotiations broke down, and the fighting in Kashmir went on.

1949.01.d: The Huaihai Campaign ended on 10 January with the capture of Du Yuming; Tianjin was liberated on the 15th, Fu Zuoyi accepted peaceful reorganization, and Beiping was peacefully liberated on the 31st; the three great campaigns ended in victory. On the 21st Chiang Kai-shek “retired”, Li Zongren became Acting President, and the KMT and CPC moved towards peace talks; Suiyuan was held together by Dong Qiwu. Meanwhile India and Pakistan agreed a ceasefire in Kashmir, the Netherlands' second “police action” brought pressure from the United Nations, and Israel and Egypt held armistice negotiations.
1949.01.t: Pingjin Campaign · Peaceful liberation of Beiping

1949.04.d: The KMT government refused to sign the Agreement on Internal Peace reached in the Beiping peace talks; on the night of 20 April the Yangtze River Crossing Campaign began, and Nanjing was liberated on the 23rd: the KMT regime that had ruled China for 22 years was overthrown (the Executive Yuan of the KMT government had already moved to Guangzhou in February); Taiyuan was liberated on the 24th, Yan Xishan having flown out in March. The British warship Amethyst intruded into the Yangtze front and exchanged fire with the People's Liberation Army. Meanwhile the North Atlantic Treaty was signed, and the Republic of Indonesia and the Netherlands resumed negotiations.
1949.04.t: Yangtze River Crossing Campaign · Liberation of Nanjing

1949.05.d: Hangzhou, Wuhan, Nanchang and Xi'an were liberated one after another; after the Shanghai Campaign, Shanghai was liberated on 27 May, and Tang Enbo's forces withdrew to Zhoushan and Taiwan. Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia and Shanxi-Suiyuan were merged into the Northwest Liberated Area, and the Central Plains Provisional People's Government was seated at Kaifeng. Martial law was imposed in Taiwan on 20 May. Meanwhile Israel joined the United Nations, and Siam changed its name back to Thailand.

1949.08.d: On 4 August Cheng Qian and Chen Mingren declared an uprising by circular telegram in Changsha, and Changsha was peacefully liberated; after the Fu-Mei Campaign, Lanzhou was liberated and the main force of Ma Bufang's group was wiped out; Fuzhou and Qingdao were liberated; the Northeast People's Government was established. The United States issued its white paper on relations with China. Meanwhile the Soviet Union tested an atomic bomb, and the Hague Round Table Conference opened to discuss the transfer of sovereignty to Indonesia.

1949.10.d: On 1 October the People's Republic of China was proclaimed in Beijing. Dong Qiwu in Suiyuan and Tao Zhiyue and Burhan Shahidi in Xinjiang declared uprisings by circular telegram, and Suiyuan and Xinjiang were peacefully liberated; Ningxia, Qinghai and Hexi were liberated; the Hengyang–Baoqing Campaign dealt a heavy blow to Bai Chongxi's group, Guangzhou was liberated on the 14th, and the KMT government moved to Chongqing; in the Battle of Kinmen the troops that crossed the sea and landed on the island were entirely lost. Meanwhile the Soviet Union, Mongolia and other countries recognized New China, and the Hague Round Table Conference went on to settle the transfer of sovereignty to Indonesia.
1949.10.t: Founding of the People's Republic of China

1949.12.d: In the Guangxi Campaign and the Southwest Campaign, Guiyang, Chongqing, Nanning and Chengdu were liberated one after another, and Lu Han in Kunming and Liu Wenhui and others at Pengxian declared uprisings by circular telegram; on 7 December the KMT authorities decided to move to Taipei and retreated to Taiwan, while the remnants of Hu Zongnan's forces fell back to hold Xichang and Xue Yue held Hainan. Mao Zedong went to Moscow to negotiate a new treaty. Meanwhile the Netherlands transferred sovereignty to the Republic of the United States of Indonesia, and the Indian Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution.
1949.12.t: Liberation of the Southwest · KMT retreats to Taiwan

1950.05.d: In February the Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance was signed; in March Chiang Kai-shek resumed office in Taipei, and Xichang was liberated; the Hainan Island Campaign ended on 1 May with the liberation of the whole of Hainan Island, and in mid-May the KMT forces withdrew from Zhoushan, thereafter falling back on Taiwan, Kinmen, Matsu and other islands. Military and administrative committees were set up in the major regions, and preparations were made to extend land reform. Meanwhile China and the Soviet Union recognized the Democratic Republic of Vietnam, the Republic of India was established, and South Korea held National Assembly elections.
1950.05.t: Liberation of Hainan Island and Zhoushan

1950.08.d: On 25 June the Korean civil war broke out; the United States intervened by armed force and on the 27th sent the Seventh Fleet to intrude into the Taiwan Strait, and the People's Liberation Army's plan to liberate Taiwan had to be shelved; the Agrarian Reform Law was promulgated in June, and the Wanshan Islands Campaign ended in August. The Southwest Military and Administrative Committee was established; negotiations over Xizang came to nothing. Meanwhile the Korean People's Army advanced to the Nakdong River, and the US-led “UN Command” forces fell back to the Busan Perimeter.

1950.10.d: In the Qamdo Campaign of 6–24 October the main force of the Tibetan army was wiped out, the Governor-General of Qamdo, Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme, laid down arms with his troops, and Qamdo was liberated; on 19 October the Chinese People's Volunteers entered Korea to fight, and the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea began. Meanwhile, after landing at Incheon in September, the “UN Command” forces crossed the 38th parallel and occupied Pyongyang; in the Border Campaign in Vietnam the French lost Cao Bằng and Lạng Sơn.

1950.12.d: The 14th Dalai Lama of Xizang assumed personal rule ahead of time in November and in December left for Yadong; the Kashag of Xizang “appealed” to the United Nations, but the appeal was not taken up. Land reform and the suppression of counter-revolutionaries were carried out across the country, and the Movement to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea was launched. The Taiwan authorities introduced local self-government. Meanwhile in the Second Campaign the CPV drove back the “UN Command” forces at the Chongchon River and Changjin Lake and recovered Pyongyang on 6 December, and the “UN Command” forces withdrew south of the 38th parallel.

1951.01.d: The whole country mobilized around the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, and land reform and the suppression of counter-revolutionaries advanced in the newly liberated areas; on 1 January the Qamdo Area People's Liberation Committee was set up, while the Dalai Lama stayed at Yadong, watching events. The Chinese government rejected the UN General Assembly's plan for a ceasefire first and negotiations afterwards. In Korea, in the Third Campaign the CPV and the Korean People's Army took Seoul on 4 January, and the “UN Command” forces fell back to the Pyeongtaek–Jecheon–Samcheok line, the ROK government moving to Busan; from the 25th Ridgway launched a counter-attack and retook Suwon. The US special envoy Dulles visited Japan to prepare a peace settlement with Japan. In mid-January the Vietnam People's Army attacked Vĩnh Yên northwest of Hà Nội in force but was beaten back by the French with air power and napalm, and the French then built the De Lattre Line along the outer edge of the Red River Delta; the South Maluku remnants retreated into the forests and mountains of Seram to wage guerrilla war.

1951.03.d: In February the Regulations on the Punishment of Counter-revolutionaries were promulgated, and the campaign to suppress counter-revolutionaries reached its climax; on 1 February the UN General Assembly, manipulated by the United States, adopted a resolution slanderously branding China an “aggressor”. In February India illegally occupied Tawang; the Chinese government has never recognized the illegal “McMahon Line”. The Dalai Lama and the Kashag decided to negotiate with the Central People's Government and appointed Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme chief delegate. In Korea, after the battles of Hoengseong and Jipyeong-ri in February, the CPV switched to mobile defence in the Fourth Campaign; in March the “UN Command” forces advanced north in Operation Ripper, retook Seoul on 14–15 March and by the end of the month were back near the 38th parallel. The Vietnam People's Army turned to attack the coal-mining district of Mạo Khê on the northeastern edge of the Delta, but repeated assaults failed to take it; in Nepal a coalition government was formed in February, ending more than a century of hereditary prime-ministerial rule by the Rana family; in March the Iranian parliament passed the nationalization of oil.

1951.06.d: The Xizang delegation arrived in Beijing in late April, and on 23 May the Agreement of the Central People's Government and the Local Government of Xizang on Measures for the Peaceful Liberation of Xizang was signed: Xizang was peacefully liberated, the Local Government of Xizang came under the unified leadership of the Central Government, and the Kashag continued to handle internal affairs; the Taiwan authorities refused to recognize the agreement. In May the United States set up a Military Assistance Advisory Group in Taipei. In Korea, MacArthur was dismissed on 11 April; from the 22nd came the Fifth Campaign, with battles on the Imjin River and at Gapyeong and Hyeon-ri; in late May the “UN Command” forces counter-attacked, and by mid-June the front had stabilized along the Imjin River–Cheorwon–Gimhwa–Yanggu–Ganseong line; on the 23rd the Soviet Union proposed ceasefire negotiations. In May–June the Vietnam People's Army crossed the Đáy River to attack the Ninh Bình line and was checked again, ending its attempts to attack the Delta; in Iran Mosaddegh became Prime Minister and took over the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company.

1951.10.d: The Dalai Lama returned to Lhasa on 17 August and on 24 October telegraphed Mao Zedong to express his support for the Agreement; the Xinjiang cavalry advance company moved into Gartok in August, and the advance detachment of the 18th Army entered Lhasa on 9 September and its main force on 26 October. The Hunan–Guangxi Railway reached Zhennan Pass. In Korea, armistice negotiations opened at Kaesong on 10 July, were broken off in August and resumed at Panmunjom on 25 October; in the meantime the “UN Command” forces fought for Bloody Ridge and Heartbreak Ridge, and the front moved north only slightly. On 8 September the United States, excluding China, signed the San Francisco Peace Treaty and the US–Japan Security Treaty with Japan; the Soviet Union refused to sign. King Abdullah of Jordan was assassinated in Jerusalem in July, and in October Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan of Pakistan was assassinated; British personnel withdrew from Abadan; Gurney, the British High Commissioner in Malaya, was killed in an ambush; the United States and the Philippines concluded a Mutual Defense Treaty.

1952.04.d: From the end of 1951 the Three-Anti and Five-Anti Campaigns were carried out. In Xizang the two Sitsab, Lukhangwa and Lobsang Tashi, were dismissed in April, and the 10th Panchen Lama arrived in Lhasa on 28 April. On the same day the Taiwan authorities signed a so-called “peace treaty” with Japan, which the Chinese government refused to recognize. In Korea, after agreement was reached in the armistice negotiations on the military demarcation line, the talks deadlocked over the repatriation of prisoners of war; China and Korea exposed the US use of germ weapons, which the United States denied. On 28 April the San Francisco Peace Treaty came into force: Japan regained its sovereignty and the Allied occupation ended, while Okinawa and the Ogasawara Islands remained under US administration; the Tokara Islands had been returned earlier, in February. French paratroops had landed at Hòa Bình in November 1951; the Vietnam People's Army besieged them for three months, and the French withdrew in February; India's first general election ended in a sweeping victory for the Congress Party; the Bengali Language Movement erupted in Dacca; Turkey joined NATO.
1952.04.t: Three-Anti and Five-Anti Campaigns · Panchen Lama returns to Xizang

1952.11.d: The Chengdu–Chongqing Railway opened to traffic in July and the Tianshui–Lanzhou Railway in October; the Three-Anti and Five-Anti Campaigns ended, and land reform was basically completed. The People's Government of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region moved to Guisui. In September China and the Soviet Union agreed that the Chinese Changchun Railway would be handed over at the end of the year and that the Soviet troops at Lüshun would stay on for an extended period. In November Pingyuan and Chahar provinces were abolished, and the major regions were reorganized under administrative committees. In October KMT forces raided Nanri Island and then withdrew. In Korea, the Panmunjom talks were adjourned indefinitely on 8 October; in the Battle of Shangganling in October–November the CPV held their positions, fierce fighting raged at White Horse Hill, and the front line remained unchanged. In October Japan's National Police Reserve was reorganized as the National Safety Force. In October the Vietnam People's Army launched the Northwest Campaign, taking Nghĩa Lộ and Sơn La, and the French fell back on the fortified camp at Nà Sản and on Lai Châu; the French Operation Lorraine pushed north to Phú Thọ but came back empty-handed; Saudi Arabia sent men to occupy the Buraimi Oasis, sparking a dispute.

1953.04.d: The Soviet Union handed over the Chinese Changchun Railway on 31 December 1952; from 1953 the First Five-Year Plan was implemented, and large-scale economic construction centred on Soviet-aided projects got under way. In February US President Eisenhower announced that the Seventh Fleet would no longer “neutralize” the Taiwan Strait. Stalin died on 5 March. In Korea, at the end of March China and Korea agreed to exchange sick and wounded prisoners of war first; the exchange took place at Panmunjom from 20 April, and the talks resumed on the 26th. In Japan the Yoshida cabinet dissolved the House of Representatives in March, and after the April general election Yoshida Shigeru continued as Prime Minister. In April the Vietnam People's Army and the Pathet Lao pushed into Upper Laos; the French and Lao garrison abandoned Sam Neua, and the Vietnamese army reached the Plain of Jars and the outskirts of Luang Prabang, while Souphanouvong's Resistance Government remained at Sam Neua; Burma took the question of the KMT remnant troops to the United Nations.
1953.04.t: First Five-Year Plan · Vietnamese army enters Upper Laos

1953.07.d: At the end of June the first national census was conducted. On 16–18 July a KMT force of nearly 10,000 men raided Dongshan Island in southern Fujian and was driven back; after this there were no more large-scale raids on the mainland. In Korea, the agreement on the repatriation of prisoners of war was signed on 8 June; on the 18th Syngman Rhee, under the guise of “releasing them on the spot”, held back more than 20,000 Korean People's Army prisoners of war, sabotaging the agreement; on 13 July the CPV launched the Battle of Kumsong, straightening out the salient south of Kumsong; on the 27th the Armistice Agreement was signed at Panmunjom, and the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea ended in victory. The agreement separated North and South by a military demarcation line and a demilitarized zone; Kaesong went to the North, while Cheorwon, Yanggu, Ganseong and other places north of the 38th parallel went to the South. Navarre took command of the French forces in Indochina in May, and the Vietnam People's Army withdrew from Upper Laos before the rainy season; Sihanouk left for Bangkok and Siem Reap, launching the “Royal Crusade” for independence; King Hussein of Jordan assumed personal rule.
1953.07.t: Victory in the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea

1953.12.d: In December the CPC Central Committee published the general line for the transition period, and the cooperative transformation of agriculture and the transformation of private industry and commerce began to speed up; on 31 December China and India opened negotiations in Beijing on relations between the Xizang Region of China and India. In Korea, the repatriation of prisoners of war by both sides was completed in September, and those unwilling to be repatriated were handed over to the custody of the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission; the ROK government moved back to Seoul in August, and on 1 October the US–ROK Mutual Defense Treaty was signed. On 25 December the Amami Islands were returned to Japan, while Okinawa and the Ogasawara Islands remained under US administration. In August a coup in Iran overthrew Mosaddegh; Laos and Cambodia became fully independent in October–November; the French dropped paratroops on Điện Biên Phủ in November and abandoned Lai Châu in December, and the Vietnam People's Army pushed into Central Laos as far as Thakhek; the KMT remnant troops began to be evacuated to Taiwan; Ibn Saud died.
1953.12.t: General Line · Cambodian and Laotian independence

1954.05.d: After the Fourth Plenary Session of the Seventh CPC Central Committee in February, Gao Gang's and Rao Shushi's activities to split the Party were exposed and criticized; Dihua was renamed Urumqi. In the spring Suiyuan Province was abolished and merged into the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, and in April Guisui was renamed Hohhot. On 26 April the Geneva Conference opened, with Zhou Enlai leading the Chinese delegation; on the 29th China and India signed the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Xizang Region of China and India, which for the first time incorporated the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence. In Korea, discussion of Korean reunification at the Geneva Conference reached deadlock. In March Japan signed the US–Japan Mutual Defense Assistance Agreement, and the Lucky Dragon No. 5 was contaminated by fallout from a hydrogen bomb test at Bikini Atoll. In January–February the Vietnam People's Army again entered Upper Laos and took Kon Tum, and the French landed at Tuy Hòa; in the Điện Biên Phủ Campaign from 13 March to 7 May the Vietnam People's Army won a great victory and the French garrison surrendered; the KMT remnant troops were evacuated to Taiwan in batches; the five-nation Colombo Conference proposed convening an Asian–African Conference.
1954.05.t: Victory at Điện Biên Phủ · Five Principles

1954.07.d: On 19 June the Central People's Government Council decided to abolish the administrative bodies at the level of the major regions; Liaodong and Liaoxi were merged into Liaoning, and Songjiang was merged into Heilongjiang. In late June Zhou Enlai visited India and Burma, and together with Nehru and U Nu advocated the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence; on 21 July the Geneva Conference reached the agreements on the cessation of hostilities in Indochina, restoring peace in Indochina. In Korea, the Geneva Conference's discussion of the Korean question broke down on 15 June, and North and South remained in a state of armistice. On 1 July Japan set up the Defense Agency and the Ground, Maritime and Air Self-Defense Forces. In June France and Vietnam initialled a treaty of independence, and Ngô Đình Diệm formed a cabinet; French Groupement Mobile 100 was destroyed at Mang Yang Pass; on 21 July the Geneva Accords set the Bến Hải River, near the 17th parallel, as the provisional military demarcation line, with the forces of both sides to regroup in separate zones within 300 days, and the Pathet Lao to regroup in Sam Neua and Phongsaly.

1954.12.d: On 3 September the People's Liberation Army shelled Kinmen (the September 3 Bombardment), and the first Taiwan Strait crisis broke out; on 2 December the United States and the Taiwan authorities signed the so-called “Mutual Defense Treaty”, whose text did not expressly cover Kinmen, Matsu or the Dachen Islands. In September the First National People's Congress adopted the Constitution of the People's Republic of China and set up the State Council; Khrushchev visited China, and it was agreed that Soviet troops would withdraw from Lüshun the following year. The abolition of the major regions was completed. On 25 December the Xikang–Xizang and Qinghai–Xizang Highways opened to traffic to Lhasa. In Korea, in November administrative authority over the “recovered areas” north of the 38th parallel was transferred to the ROK, and the US–ROK treaty came into force. In Japan Yoshida Shigeru fell from power in December, and Hatoyama Ichirō formed a cabinet. The Vietnam People's Army took over Hà Nội in October and the central organs of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam moved back, while large numbers of northern residents moved south via Hải Phòng; in September the Manila Pact was signed; Dadra and Nagar Haveli broke away from Portugal, and French India was transferred de facto in November; the Bogor Conference decided to convene the Asian–African Conference.
1954.12.t: First National People's Congress · September 3 Bombardment
